## 1. Mode, task type and rule bundle

`IMPLEMENTATION`, governance tooling (a new rendered gate and its registry); no product UI, Story or token changes.
Bundles: **Storybook / Visual Proof**, **Regression / Critical Flow Coverage** (gate with planted-failure proof).
Read: `.claude/rules/shared/role-boundaries.md`, `.claude/rules/shared/rendered-state-census.md` (the contract this
task implements), `.claude/rules/shared/mobile-adaptation-contract.md` ("Required decision and proof"),
`docs/qa-profiles.md`, `docs/storybook-governance.md` §14.9.18 (the retired overlay click list, for contrast only).

## 2. Objective

The owner rejected a task-local fix for a census that could not see dialogs (D1). Build the project-wide contract
`rendered-state-census.md` as executable tooling: a registry of every interaction state that opens a portal, a runner
that opens each state on the built Storybook and measures the app root and every portal root separately, JSONL
evidence per Story × state × root × locale × viewport, and a self-test whose planted violations live only inside a
portal while the app root is green.

## 3. Verified context

Every fact below is a ledger row; nothing else sets scope.

- Mantine renders every overlay into `<div data-portal="true">` under `<body>` (C1). Both GR-3j censuses of 859 read
  `#storybook-root` only (C2): the app root was green (C3) while the ticket sheet header was squeezed (C4) and a picker
  name rendered one letter per line with the id past the screen (C5).
- The repository's only overlay-opening rendered tool is the retired `screenshots:assert` engine (C6); it clicks the
  first button or input of the app root (C7) and measures nothing per portal. It is not revived or extended here.
- A Story can need a click to open its overlay: `Mantine/Primitives/Modal` `Default` shows no dialog on mount (C8).
- CI already builds Storybook and runs rendered gates with a self-test (C9, C10, C11). Playwright and Storybook are
  installed (C12, C13).
- Overlay owners are registered as the `overlay-and-disclosure` family (C14); the touch token is 44px (C15).
- Legacy components are migrated, not instrumented (C16): the registry covers `Mantine/Primitives/*` and
  `Patterns/Mantine/*` Stories only.

| D24 | OWNER DECISION | Tables become cards only below 640px, like every other compact presentation. | owner: 2026-10-17; decision: `Tables too, from 640px` |
| D25 | OWNER DECISION | Deleting an account (by staff or by the person) removes every piece of information about it. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `An account deleted by an admin or by the user themselves deletes all information about the account in the system. … Deletion is deletion!` |
| D26 | OWNER DECISION | A ban ends access at once, not after the token lifetime. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `Of course, shorten the token lifetime to 0 seconds!` |
| D27 | OWNER DECISION | D25 and D26 hold for every account and every role (user, agent, moderator, administrator), on every layer. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `This applies to all users, not only the administrator! … if a user is deleted, all information about them is deleted. If a user is blocked, they become blocked immediately!` |
| D28 | OWNER DECISION | An account marked by the inactivity rule has no access until it returns; within 90 days it is restored as today; after 90 days it is deleted completely, as D25. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `90 days to restore, then full deletion` |
| D29 | OWNER DECISION | A blocked person's open session is ended by the server at once; the person sees the site as a guest. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `The server ends the session; it becomes a guest` |
| D30 | OWNER DECISION | Every account deletion, by the person or by staff, is a complete hard delete of the account, its data, its listings and their Cloudinary images, for every role, after a warning modal. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `Let us do a hard delete everywhere after all. … There is no point in keeping the data of a user who deleted their account, or whose account an admin/moderator deleted. This applies to all users (user/realtor/moderator/admin).` |
| D31 | OWNER DECISION | A company is created only by a signed-in, confirmed agent in the cabinet; the sign-up only picks an existing one; the company is deleted with its creator and its other agents are left without it. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `do not allow creating a company until the user signs in … This way we can track who created the company and delete it together with the owner. Other agents who joined this company are left without a company` |
| D32 | OWNER DECISION | A record of a staff member's action keeps the staff member's name and id; when the staff member is deleted the record stays with the name only. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `The record must keep the user's name and ID. If this admin/moderator was deleted, the record must remain, but only with the user's name, without the ID` |
| D33 | OWNER DECISION | The person's views and clicks on others' listings are deleted with the account; the reports and inquiries the person filed are kept for staff to moderate. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `The owner's statistics are deleted, there is no point for us in keeping them. Complaints and requests are kept, because there may be a fraud scheme` |
| D34 | OWNER DECISION | Deletion asks the person to type DELETE both in the cabinet and in the admin panel. | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `Type DELETE in both places` |
| D35 | OWNER DECISION | Every record kept after an account is deleted keeps the account's name (the reports included). | owner: 2026-10-18; decision: `I told you directly - we keep the account name.` |

## Mobile adaptation record
- Scope: visible
- Surfaces: src/modules/listings/components/ListingInquiryDialogView.tsx — the message dialog of the listing contact card (R41); src/modules/listings/components/ListingFormShellView.tsx — the status field of the listing edit form (R35); the sign-in sheet's error text (R40, no layout change); the admin record tables of AdminListingsView, AdminCurrenciesView, AdminReportsView, AdminPagesView, AdminExchangeProvidersView and the AdminSurfacePattern, the admin listings visibility filter and the listings filter close control (R39); src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineDeleteConfirmModal.tsx with its typed confirmation, consumed by src/modules/cabinet/components/ProfileTab.tsx (the self-deletion dialog) and src/components/admin/AdminUserProfileDialogsView.tsx (the admin deletion dialog) (R46); src/modules/cabinet/components/CabinetEmailChangeSectionView.tsx — the e-mail change section of the cabinet profile tab (R83); src/modules/listings/components/ListingAccessRestrictedView.tsx — the restricted-listing page: breadcrumb band, then the empty state's icon, title, text and one action (R103); src/modules/listings/components/ListingFormShellView.tsx — the price field's input mode and digit parsing (R102, behaviour only, no layout change); src/components/admin/AdminPageHeader.tsx — the notice under the admin page header of the Users list, after a deleted user's page (R139)
- Component families: overlay-and-disclosure, form-picker-and-choice, record-list-and-data, filter-and-action-toolbar, structural-layout-and-feedback, media-gallery-and-listing-contact
- Pattern IDs: overlay-adaptive, form-stack, data-table-to-cards, record-card, toolbar-priority, key-value-stack, linear-flow, inline-control
- Standards: w3c-focus-order, w3c-hover-focus, apple-hig-sheets, android-common-layouts, android-adapt-layouts, w3c-labels-instructions, w3c-reflow, apple-hig-layout, android-content-structure, w3c-meaningful-sequence, apple-hig-lists-tables, apple-hig-toolbars, android-layout-navigation, android-layout-basics, w3c-target-size, apple-hig-menus
- Mantine mechanism: media-query-exception, responsive-props, visibility-props
- Mantine owner: src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineModal.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineDrawer.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineSelect.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineDataTableToCards.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineAdminSurfacePattern.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineDetailList.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineEmptyLoadingErrorState.tsx, src/design-system/mantine/patterns/MantineDashboardHeader.tsx
- Mobile range and switches: the restricted page (R103) has no threshold of its own: below 640px (sm) its one action is full width by the caller's `{ base: '100%', sm: 'auto' }` (as `FavoritesShell`), from 640 it takes its own width, and the page frame's gutter steps at its existing breakpoints; the price field (R102) changes no layout. Otherwise: below 640px (theme.other.mobileGate / sm) `MantineModal` shows its bottom sheet, `MantineDialogFooter` its full-width pair, the admin pagination its compact size, the listings visibility filter its select and the listings filter panel its close icon and Apply button (mounted only in `MantineDrawer`'s bottom-sheet presentation, R48); the 640px transition shows the centred modal, the wide pagination and the segmented filter. Tables (D36, Revision 9, replacing D24 for tables): below 768px (`md`) every table shows its record cards, so 640–767 keeps the cards; from 768 the table shows and must fit (§7.3); `AgentStatisticsView` keeps its 1024 (`lg`) exception; no other threshold The human check (R113) has no threshold of its own: it takes no space until Cloudflare asks for interaction, then shows Cloudflare's compact 150 × 140 box at every width (the contact card is 246px wide at 320, C1029).
- Mobile order: dialog title; name; e-mail; message; Cancel then Send — status field: label; select; note; save — record card: identity, state, details, actions (as `MantineDataTableToCards` cards today) — admin listings filter: status select, then visibility select — deletion dialog: title; consequence text; typed-word field with its label; Cancel then Delete — e-mail section (R83): title; current e-mail, label then value; then the waiting notice, the error when a resend was refused, and the resend action at the start of its line (R138), or the error, the new e-mail field with its label and hint, the current password, the full-width submit; then the Google control — restricted page (R103): breadcrumb; icon; title; text; the one action — contact card (R113): agent; price; Call, WhatsApp; the human check when shown; Send message; save; report — message dialog (R113): name; e-mail; message; the human check when shown; Cancel then Send — Users list header (R139): title; the total and New user; the notice; then the table
- Required-content treatment: wrap — titles, labels, placeholders and merged meta lines wrap inside their cell; no clipping, no semantic loss
- Story and verification: src/stories/patterns/mantine/ListingInquiryDialogView.stories.tsx, the existing patterns-mantine-statuschangeselect Stories and the default Stories of the five admin Views and AdminSurfacePattern, and for R46 src/stories/mantine/primitives/Modal.stories.tsx DeleteConfirmTyped with the AdminUserProfileDialogsView Delete Story, for R48 src/stories/patterns/mantine/ListingsFilters.stories.tsx Default, for R49 src/stories/mantine/primitives/Table.stories.tsx Default, CardsBelowMd and CardsBelowLg; 320, 390, 639, 640, 641, 700, 767, 768, 769 and 1440; sq, en, uk, it; for R83 src/stories/patterns/mantine/CabinetEmailChangeSectionView.stories.tsx, all 11 exports, at 320, 390, 639, 640, 768, 1024 and 1440 in sq, en, uk and it; for R103 src/stories/patterns/mantine/ListingAccessRestrictedView.stories.tsx Guest and SignedIn at 320, 390, 639, 640, 767, 768, 1024 and 1440 in sq, en, uk and it, and the route on the local site (§54.5); for R113 src/stories/patterns/mantine/ListingContactPattern.stories.tsx, src/stories/patterns/mantine/ListingInquiryDialogView.stories.tsx and src/stories/patterns/mantine/AuthSheet.stories.tsx Captcha, all unchanged, and the route on the local site at 320, 360, 390, 639, 640, 1024 and 1440 in sq, en, uk and it (§57, r33-08); for R139 src/stories/patterns/mantine/AdminPageHeader.stories.tsx Default, WithAction and WithNotice at 320, 375, 390, 480, 560, 639, 640, 641, 680, 768, 810, 960, 1024, 1200, 1440, 1920 and 2560 in sq, en, uk and it

## 4. Scope and out of scope

**In scope (the exact write set):**
`scripts/check-rendered-state-census.mjs` (runner, CLI, self-test) and, if it is split, modules under
`scripts/rendered-state-census/`; `scripts/rendered-interaction-states.json` (registry);
`scripts/__fixtures__/rendered-state-census/*.html` (self-test fixtures); `scripts/__tests__/rendered-state-census.test.ts`
(registry validator unit tests); `package.json` (three script entries only); evidence `docs/sessions/evidence/task923/*`;
the session log `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`; the 923 backlog cell.

**Out of scope:** any product source, Story, fixture, theme or token file (an overlay that cannot be opened without
editing its Story is reported, not repaired); `scripts/check-stories-rendered.mjs` and every retired alias (C6);
legacy Stories (C16); the CI workflow and the policy documents (Opus adds the CI steps and the governance doc rows at
review closure, §9); fixing any violation the gate finds (each is owned by a numbered task, R9).

## 5. Current and required behaviour

| | Current | Required |
|---|---|---|
| Overlay states | opened ad hoc by task probes, often not at all | every opening state registered and opened by the gate |
| Roots measured | `#storybook-root` only (C2) | the app root and each `[data-portal="true"]` root, separately |
| Text | clamp / ellipsis / overflow in the app root | the same per root, plus a word split across lines (C19) |
| Proof of the gate | none | planted portal-only violations fail while the app root is green |

## Requirements

| ID | Observable requirement | P | AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 [C1; C8; C14; C16; C17; D1] | **Registry** `scripts/rendered-interaction-states.json`: `{ "version": 1, "states": [...] }`; each state `{ id, story, open, portals, focus, dismiss, trigger?, closeSelector?, reason?, ownerDecision? }`. `story` = a Storybook id whose title starts `Mantine/Primitives/` or `Patterns/Mantine/`; `open` = `{ "kind": "mount" }`, `{ "kind": "click", "selector": "<css inside #storybook-root>" }` or `{ "kind": "keys", "selector": "…", "keys": ["ArrowDown"] }`; `portals` ≥ 1; `focus` = `trap` (Modal, Drawer, bottom sheet), `trigger` (focus stays on the trigger: Combobox / Select dropdown, Tooltip) or `inside` (Menu); `dismiss` ⊆ `escape`, `close-control`, `outside` — empty only with a `reason` (e.g. a View Story whose `onClose` is a no-op); `trigger` = the selector focus returns to (absent for `mount`). `id` unique; the validator rejects an unknown key, a duplicate id, a Story id absent from the build index and an out-of-scope title. | P1 | AC2 |
| R2 [C1; C14; C16; D1] | **Discovery** `--discover` on the built Storybook: every in-scope Story opened closed at 390 / en; reports (a) a Story that shows a `[data-portal="true"]` root on mount with no `mount` row, (b) an in-scope Story whose `importPath` file imports `Modal`, `Drawer`, `Popover`, `Menu`, `Combobox`, `Select`, `Tooltip` or `HoverCard` from `@mantine/core`, or any member of the `overlay-and-disclosure` family, `MantineCombobox`, `MantineSelect` or `RangeDatePicker`, with no row. The executor populates the registry until both lists are empty, reading each Story's source for its real triggers. | P1 | AC2 |
| R3 [C9; C12; C13; C18; D1] | **Runner** `check-rendered-state-census.mjs`: serves `storybook-static` read-only; for each registry state × locale × viewport (default widths 320 / 390 / 639 / 640 / 1440, locales sq / en / uk / it; `--stories <id,…>`, `--widths`, `--locales` narrow a run for a task) opens the state through its `open` action (never by editing a Story), asserts exactly `portals` new `[data-portal="true"]` roots with visible content, then measures the app root and each portal root as separate targets (the metrics of the next row); also sweeps every in-scope Story closed at 390 / en for an unregistered portal. Exit 1 on any violation, any open failure or any unregistered portal; exit 0 only when every job passes. | P1 | AC3 |
| R4 [C15; C18; C19; D1] | **Metrics per target**, each a named rule: `text-clamp` (computed `-webkit-line-clamp` ≠ none on a visible text element); `text-ellipsis` (`text-overflow: ellipsis` with hidden/clip overflow and `white-space: nowrap`, or active overflow); `text-hidden` (hidden/clip overflow with scroll size > client size + 0.5); `word-split` (a text element narrower than its longest word, measured with the element's computed font); `viewport-overflow` (page horizontal scroll, or the target's box past the viewport); `component-overflow` (an element whose box extends past its nearest clipping or target ancestor by > 0.5px, inside no scroll region that contains it); `action-hidden` / `action-covered` (a button, link with an icon, input, select or `[role=button]` outside the viewport and every scroll region, or not the hit element at its centre); `target-small` (below 768px: an action's smaller side < 44px, inline text links excluded); `focus-*` (`trap` / `inside`: on open the active element is inside the portal root, and for `trap` 1 + n Tab and Shift+Tab presses keep it inside; `trigger`: it stays on the trigger); `dismiss-*` (per declared mechanism: the portal content is hidden within 1 s and, for `trap` / `inside` with a `trigger`, focus returns to it). | P1 | AC3, AC4 |
| R5 [D1] | **Evidence**: one JSONL row per Story × state × root × locale × viewport: `{ story, state, root: "app" \| "portal:<n>", locale, width, rules: { <rule>: [<detail>] }, pass }`; a summary file with per-rule and per-Story × state counts. Paths from `--out`. | P1 | AC3 |

The output names every case and its rule; exit 0 only when every case behaves as stated. | P1 | AC1 |

The run is expected to exit 1; the report is the deliverable, never a reason to weaken a rule. | P1 | AC4 |

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 [R6; C20; D1].** `npm run check:rendered-state-census:verify` exit 0; the transcript lists `clean` PASS and each of the eight planted cases FAIL with the rule named in R6.
- **AC2 [R1; R2; C17].** `npm run check:rendered-state-census:discover` on the final build: 0 Stories with an unregistered mount portal, 0 overlay-importing in-scope Stories without a row; the registry validator accepts the saved registry; the registry row count and the per-family counts are in the report.
- **AC3 [R3; R4; R5; C18].** The full run on the final build writes one JSONL row per Story × state × root × locale × viewport (row count = the product the summary prints), every row carries every R4 rule key, 0 jobs fail to open.
- **AC4 [R4; R9; C4; C5].** In the first full run, `patterns-mantine-ticketdetaildialogview--support` at 320 / 390 reports a violation on its portal root, `patterns-mantine-userpickerfieldview--results` at 320 reports `word-split` and `viewport-overflow` on its portal root while its app root passes, `patterns-mantine-listingpreviewdialogview--active` at 320 reports `text-clamp` on its portal root; every violation is listed with an owner.
- **AC5 [R7; R8; C11].** The three scripts exist; vitest twice green (the new test file included); `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `build-storybook`, `check:file-integrity`, `check:mojibake` exit 0.

## 6. Flows

**Positive:** build Storybook → `--discover` (empty) → full run → JSONL + summary → `--verify-gate` green.

| Branch | Applicable? | Expected behaviour | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|
| A click selector matches nothing | Yes | the job fails `open-failed` with the selector | AC3 / R6 |
| A state opens more or fewer portals than declared | Yes | the job fails `portal-count` | R6 `registered-opens-nothing` |
| A Story errors on render | Yes | the job fails `error-screen` | AC3 |
| No `storybook-static` | Yes | exit 1 with "build Storybook first" | transcript |
| Validation / authorization / network / concurrent writer | No | tooling on a static build | — |

## 7. QA profile and verification

**Q4.** In order, each after the last write (`r1-60-hashes-end.txt`): `npm run build-storybook`;
`check:rendered-state-census:discover`; `check:rendered-state-census -- --out docs/sessions/evidence/task923/full`;
`check:rendered-state-census:verify`; vitest twice; `typecheck`; `lint`; `build`; `check:file-integrity`;
`check:mojibake`; `git status --porcelain` before and after. Each transcript ends with `EXIT_CODE=`. Platform line
(`win32`, Node version) first. Runtime of the full run is recorded (CI job budget).

## 8. Completion report

Session log with: I0 hashes; the registry summary; R1–R9 → evidence; AC1–AC5 with transcripts; the first-run
violation table with owners; deviations; a `Files Changed` table. Status: `IMPLEMENTED - AWAITING ORCHESTRATOR
REVIEW`, `PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED` or `BLOCKED`. No Git. A Story that cannot be opened without editing it, or a rule
that cannot be measured as written, is a stop and report, not a local reinterpretation.

## 9. Opus at review closure (not the executor)

Add to `.github/workflows/governance-pr.yml`, in the job that builds Storybook (C9): `check:rendered-state-census:verify`
blocking at once; `check:rendered-state-census` blocking the day the full run is green (until then the first-run
violations are owned tasks, and the contract's per-task rule applies). Add the gate to `docs/storybook-governance.md`
and `docs/rules/golden/enforcement-status.md`.

   evidence cannot be audited.

   blocking CI gate that fails on a transient is not usable, and "run it again" is not a rule.

   with an inclusive `max-width` of the 40em gate (C43–C46). At exactly 640 that query still matches, while the

   not operable (C51). 147 are under an overlay their Story opens on mount, and one is in a Story with no mount row

## 15. Revision 6 — review 6, 2026-10-15 (`NEEDS REVISION`)

Review evidence: `docs/sessions/evidence/task923/review-6/` (native Windows, Node v22.22.3; record `rv6-00-review.md`).
Verified on the delivered files (62 of 62 hashes equal `r6-87-hashes-end.txt`): R24–R27 are in the code as written. The
self-test reproduces with 52 cases (C129), the mutation proof is 21 of 21 (C130), AC25 reproduces (C131), and AC27
reproduces on a listing over 1 MiB (C145). Every AC23–AC28 holds as written, and the executor's status was right.
D33, D35, D37 and D38 are accepted; D34 and D36 are answered by the findings below. The code of R24–R27 stays.

**Owner decision D2 (2026-10-15).** Revision 6 keeps the full run, and this section is written so that the executor
can finish it without being stopped by the kickoff and finds every defect. Revision 6 therefore removes **every** known
source of a verdict that changes between identical runs in one revision, and proves it by two full runs that agree.

### 15.1 Findings — why the verdict still moves

1. **P1 (§14 R26 (c)): dismissal is judged on speed.** Rows change verdict on `dismiss-outside` alone, in both
   directions (C132). Run alone, the same Stories show no dismissal violation (C133). The overlay always closes: in about
   310ms at CPU 1x (C134), over a second at 8x (C135). The 1 000ms bound (C136) under 10 workers (C137) judges the
   machine's load. Such a verdict can never be the blocking whole-registry step (C138).
2. **P1 (new, §3 `waitStable`): the gate measures a page that is still loading.** Every dashboard chart arrives through
   a lazy, browser-only import (C149). `waitStable` looks only at the portal count and the finite animations (C150), and
   the open action runs as soon as the load ends (C154). With the chart chunk on time, the gate measures the chart's
   three overflow details (C151). With the chunk 2 000ms late — what 10 workers on one local server do — `waitStable`
   returns first, the chart is not there yet, and the page grows from 756 to 1 145 elements after the measurement
   (C152). This is the cause of the chart rows that lose their detail between runs (C153, the executor's D34); page
   reuse and storage are ruled out (C157).
3. **P2 (§11 R16): a retry merges a different page into the row.** A retry copies the first attempt's violations and
   roots into the result (C139, C146). The first attempt never reached the state: its open failed (C140), so its app
   root was measured on the closed, non-inert page (C141). 16 rows of the Revision 4 full run say "not measured" and
   carry violations at once (C142). The unit test pins that behaviour (C148). This is the executor's D36 (ii).
4. **P3: the R24 skip count is written as a not-applicable reason** (C143), on rows that still have violations of the
   same rule (C144).

### 15.2 Write set and out of scope

| ID | Observable requirement | P | AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| R28 [C132; C133; C134; C135; C136; C137; C138; D1; D2] | **A dismissal is judged on whether the overlay closes, not how fast.** After the dismissal action, `dismissCheck` polls the visible portal count every 50ms until it is 0, bounded at **5 000ms** (was 1 000ms). A failure reads `<rule>: the portal is still visible 5000ms after the dismissal`. Every row carries `dismissMs`: an object from each dismissal mechanism that ran on that row to its measured close time in ms, or `null` when the overlay did not close (`{}` on a row where none ran). Nothing else changes: the focus return still uses `settleFocus`, and no retry is added. New fixture `slow-close`, a portal dialog with a green app root (`focus: trap`, `dismiss: ["escape", "close-control", "outside"]`): each mechanism closes it 1 500ms after the event, and the portal stays visible until then. It is PASS on every rule of every root, and its `dismissMs` is at least 1 500 for each of the three mechanisms. `escape-does-not-close` stays FAIL `dismiss-escape`, with the 5 000ms detail. Mutation: the bound back to 1 000ms, and `slow-close` fails `dismiss-escape`. | P1 | AC29, AC30, AC32 |
| R29 [C139; C140; C141; C146; C147; C148] | **A retry replaces the first attempt.** When `runWithRetry` retries a job, the job's rows are the second attempt's rows only: no rule and no root of the first attempt is copied in (the merges of C139 and C146 are removed). Every row still records `retry` with the first failure, and a second failure is still the violation. R16's sentence "a retry never clears a violation of a measured rule" is replaced by **"a job is retried only for a load or open failure, never because a measured rule failed"**; `transientReason` is unchanged. The unit test of C148 is rewritten to the new rule: a first attempt with `open-failed` and `text-clamp`, then a clean second attempt, ends with no `text-clamp`, `pass: true`, and `retry` recorded. New fixture `open-flaky-once-closed-violation`: like `open-flaky-once` (the trigger is absent on the first load only), and the app root also holds a visible 20×20 button; the state is a modal dialog, so while it is open the app root's actions are not measured. It is PASS on every rule of every root, `retry` is recorded on every row, and the app row has no `target-small` detail. Mutation: the first-attempt merge put back, and the case fails `target-small` on `app`. | P2 | AC29, AC32 |
| R30 [C143; C144] | **The R24 skip count is its own key.** Every row carries `skippedActions`, a number (0 when nothing was skipped). `markSkippedActions` writes it there and no longer writes `notApplicable`. `notApplicable` keeps only the reasons why a rule was not measured on that row. In `verify.mjs`, `track-flex-synced` asserts `skippedActions` ≥ 1 on `portal:0` and no `action-*` key in that row's `notApplicable`. | P3 | AC29, AC32 |
| R31 [C149; C150; C151; C152; C153; C154; C155; C156; C157; D2] | **The gate measures a settled page.** One settle function (`waitStable`, extended) is used after the load and **before the open action** (new), after the open action (as now), when a dismissal check reopens the state (as now), and in the closed sweep (as now). The page is settled when, on **3 consecutive polls 100ms apart**, all of these hold: (a) the visible portal count is unchanged (and equals the expected count where one is given), as now; (b) no finite animation runs, as now (R26 (a)); (c) **no request from the page to the page's own origin is in flight** — counted on the Node side from the page's `request`, `requestfinished` and `requestfailed` events; a request to another origin (map tiles) is not counted; (d) **the layout signature is unchanged**: computed in `in-page.mjs` over `#storybook-root` and every visible portal root, it is the number of elements whose box is not empty plus a sum over their boxes rounded to whole pixels (left, top, width, height); an element that runs an infinite animation, and everything inside it, is left out, so a loader never holds the page. The bound is **8 000ms** (was 4 000ms). Every row records `settle: { ms, bounded }` for the settle before its measurement (`bounded: true` when the bound was hit; the page is then measured as it is). The summary prints the number of jobs that hit the bound, listed by Story × state. For the self-test, the static server delays a response by `<n>`ms when the request URL carries `__census_delay=<n>`; it still serves the file named by the path (C155). New fixtures, each a portal dialog with a green app root: `late-fetch-overflow` — on open, the dialog fetches `clean.html?__census_delay=1500`, and when the fetch ends it appends a 300px block inside a 200px `overflow: visible` box: FAIL `component-overflow` on `portal:0`. `late-fetch-inside` — the same with a 150px block: PASS on every rule of every root. `raf-grow-overflow` — on open, a block grows by `requestAnimationFrame` from 0 to 300px wide over 1 200ms inside a 200px box: FAIL `component-overflow` on `portal:0`. `raf-grow-inside` — the same, growing to 150px: PASS. `infinite-spinner-toast` (C156) stays PASS. Three mutations: drop (c), and `late-fetch-overflow` goes green; drop (d), and `raf-grow-overflow` goes green; drop the infinite-animation exclusion of (d), and `infinite-spinner-toast` fails. | P1 | AC29, AC31, AC32 |

### 15.5 How to run it so nothing gets in the way

1. Order: I0 and hashes → R29, R30, R28, R31 with their fixtures → AC29 (self-test, then mutations) → `build-storybook`
   → AC30, AC31 → `r7-full-a` → `r7-full-b` → the AC32 scripts → AC33 → session log.
2. Run each full run with `run_in_background`. While a full run or the self-test is running, run **nothing else** that
   loads the machine or writes the same evidence (no vitest, build, second census, probe). One writer per evidence file
   (the D37 overlap must not recur).
3. Every transcript starts with the platform line and the command and ends with `EXIT_CODE=`. A census run exits 1
   because of product findings; that is expected and is not a failure of the AC.
4. A new full run takes longer than Revision 5's 10 503s because pages now settle; report both runtimes.
5. Keep the exported names and arguments of `startStaticServer`, `storybookContext`, `newMeasuringPage`, `loadStory`,
   `waitStable(page, expected, timeout)`, `openAction`, `dismissCheck` and `runStateJob`: the review-6 probes import
   them and must run unchanged against the new code (AC30, AC31). A page made by `newMeasuringPage` carries the
   request counter of R31 (c) itself, so a probe needs no extra setup.
6. If an AC is not met, keep going through the rest and report each unmet AC with its evidence. A gap in this kickoff
   is reported as a question for Opus in the session log, never solved by a change outside §15.2.

**Verification order:** as §15.5, evidence prefix `r7-`. The session log gets a `# Revision 6` section with R28–R31
mapped to evidence, AC29–AC33 with transcripts, the determinism table, the owner table and deviations. Strongest status:
`IMPLEMENTED - AWAITING ORCHESTRATOR REVIEW`.

## 16. Revision 7 — review 7, 2026-10-16 (`NEEDS REVISION`)

Review evidence: `docs/sessions/evidence/task923/review-7/` (native Windows, Node v22.22.3; record `rv7-00-review.md`). Verified on the
delivered files (69 of 69 hashes equal `r7-87-hashes-end.txt`, C158): R28–R31 are in the code as written; the self-test (C159) and the
mutation proof (C160) reproduce; the determinism comparison reproduces its 4 rows that AC32 does not allow (C161). AC29, AC30, AC31 and AC33
hold; AC32 does not, and the executor's status `PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED` was right. D39, D40, D41, D44 and D45 are accepted; D42 and D43 are
answered by the findings below. The code of R28–R31 stays.

**Owner decisions D3 and D4 (2026-10-16).** A cause found by a run no longer waits for a new revision. The executor runs the registry
Story by Story, and fixes each gate defect where it finds it, under the fix contract of R33; a product race is classified and goes to the
owner table. Revision 7 therefore ends with every Story checked on the final code, not with a list of new causes for Revision 8.
**Owner decision D5 (2026-10-16), same day:** small parts, no runs that buy nothing. Only three Stories differed between the two Revision 6
full runs (C183); the other 257 agreed, so R33 runs those three only, and the one final full run is compared with `r7-full-b` — the second
run of an identical pair is no longer made. The Story pairs `r8-story/001…` already made by the first R33 loop stay as evidence; that loop
is not continued.

### 16.1 Findings — the three cells

1. **P1 (new): a same-origin stylesheet that fails is not seen, and the gate measures the broken page.** Run a's
   `admindashboardview--activity-error~about-visible-listings` uk 320 row is the row of a page without its stylesheet (C162) whose open
   opened nothing (C163). Aborting the Storybook stylesheet, or answering it 404, reproduces the row (C164, C165). The signature is in one row
   of run a and in none of run b or of the Revision 5 run (C166). `loadTarget` never checks a subresource (C167), the static server answers
   404 to every error and logs nothing (C168), and such a failure is not in the transient class (C169), so it became a set of product
   violations. Across all 260 Stories no same-origin script, stylesheet or document fails; 107 same-origin `fetch` requests (`/api/*`) answer
   404 on every load (C171), so `fetch` must stay out of the rule. This answers D43 (first cell).
2. **P2 product race, not a gate defect: the Leaflet popup.** The listing map opens its popup in the Leaflet import callback (C172) while its
   stylesheet is a cross-origin link of the same component (C173). When the chunk wins, Leaflet sizes the popup before its stylesheet applies
   and keeps 301px (C174); when the stylesheet wins, 248px (C175). The settled page never changes afterwards (C176), so no settle condition can
   see it (answers D42: no settle extension). The verdict of `listingdetailview` app rows at the widths where 248px fits and 301px does not
   follows this race (C182). It goes to the owner table.
3. **P2 product race, not a gate defect: the share tooltip.** The share button flips its tooltip label back 2 000ms after the click (C177).
   Escape before the flip closes the tooltip, which then reappears on its own (C178); Escape after it closes it for good (C179). Run a's
   Escape fell next to the flip and never saw it closed (C180); run b's came early and saw it closed (C181). It goes to the owner table
   (answers D43, second cell).

- **AC37 [R32].** The test file passes twice. `npm test` (the whole suite) is run once and kept, with AC28's treatment if it is red.
  `typecheck`, `lint`, `build`, `build-storybook`, `check:file-integrity` and `check:mojibake` exit 0. `git status --porcelain` is captured
  before and after.

### 16.5 How to run it so nothing gets in the way

1. Order: I0 and hashes → R32 (a)–(d), then its fixtures (e) → AC34 (self-test, then mutations, then the test file) → `build-storybook` →
   AC35 → R33 on the three Stories of C183 (about 5 minutes) → the final full run `r8-full`, the only long run → the AC36 scripts → AC37 →
   session log.
2. Every rule of §15.5 (2)–(6) applies unchanged, with the prefix `r8-` and the review-7 probe (AC35) in place of the review-6 ones; the exported
   names and arguments listed there stay as they are. In the loop, one thing runs at a time: a Story's run, a fix, the self-test, the mutation
   proof. A fix to the gate code needs no `build-storybook` (the Storybook build is product output and does not change).
3. Keep going. A Story whose cause is not found is outcome (iii) and the loop moves on; the loop and the final full run are never stopped for
   one Story. A defect that only a file outside the gate write set could fix is outcome (iii) with that file named, never a change to it.
4. The owner table is Revision 6's (`r7-86-…`), recomputed on `r8-full`, plus a row for every R33 outcome (ii), and these two: **the Leaflet popup race** (`src/components/shared/Map.tsx`: the popup is sized
   before its cross-origin stylesheet applies, and 301px is wider than the map at 390) and **the share tooltip that reappears after Escape**
   (`ListingShareButton`: the 2 000ms label reset reopens a dismissed tooltip under a resting pointer). Opus files them, with the rows marked
   "new" in Revision 6, at closure (§9).

**Verification order:** as §16.5, evidence prefix `r8-`. The session log gets a `# Revision 7` section with R32 and R33 mapped to evidence,
AC34–AC37 with transcripts, the iteration table, the final comparison, the owner table and deviations. Strongest status: `IMPLEMENTED - AWAITING ORCHESTRATOR REVIEW`.

### 17.3a Flows, negative branches and the visible decisions of R35 and R40–R42

**Positive flows.** (1) Staff open a listing's edit page and set any allowed status, `active` included; the gateway applies it.
(2) An owner opens their listing's edit page, sees every allowed status but `active`, sets one, and it is applied. (3) A signed-in
visitor with an active account opens the contact card's message dialog, fills it and sends; the success toast shows and the dialog
closes empty. (4) A person with valid credentials signs in through the sheet and it closes.

| Branch | Applicable? | Owner/source | Expected behavior | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Validation | Yes | dialog `canSubmit`; action `validation` | Send stays disabled until name, a plain e-mail and 20+ characters are given; a server `validation` answer shows its toast, values kept | SEC-CS-FE-*, `test:listings` |
| Authorization / session | Yes | `requireViewer`, gateway, Auth ban | `unauthenticated` → R42 path; owner → `active` refused by the gateway even if sent (SEC-D8-SRV-DENY); banned sign-in → R40 text | SEC-CS-*, SEC-D8-*, SEC-D9-* |
| Offline / network | Yes | `save_failed`, toast layer | A failed request shows `inquiry_error_save_failed`, the dialog stays open with its values | SEC-CS-FE-ERR |
| Concurrent writer | No | — | Two status changes race in the gateway as today; this revision changes who may target `active`, not concurrency | n/a |
| Unknown answer | Yes | R42 fallback | Any unrecognised `result.error` is an error toast, never success | SEC-CS-FE-ERR |

### 17.5 How to run it

1. Start in a fresh Claude Code session. Read this section, the record and the contract, then emit the contract receipt
   (`node scripts/workflow-gates/cli.mjs receipt --contract …`) before the first product edit.
2. **Executable now, in this order:** R34 → R35 (`listingStatusOptions` first, then the form, then the deletion) → R40 → R41 (View, then
   its Story and registry rows, then the container) → R42 → R36 → R38 (manifest first) → R39 → R44 (`requireViewer` first, then the
   guards, then the entry points) → R45 (a) → R37 (a) → R43 (a) inventory, then R43 (b) the deletion SQL draft and its rollback, not
   applied, with their SHA-256 for Opus's review. Before the
   first UI or Story write, emit the receipts of `shared/enforcement-model.md` with the values of §17.3a and the Mobile adaptation record;
   one mobile receipt per Mantine owner (`MantineModal.tsx` for R41, `MantineSelect.tsx` for R35, `MantineDataTableToCards.tsx` and
   `MantineAdminSurfacePattern.tsx` for R39). **Waiting on others:** R37 (b)–(e) wait for Opus's re-review and the owner's approval of the
   v4 hash (`BLOCKED — OWNER SQL APPROVAL`); R45 (b) and (c) follow R37 (d) because they call the new functions; R43 (b)–(e) and
   R45 (e) wait for Opus's review and the owner's approval of the deletion SQL; R46 (a) and (b) are executable now, and (c) and (d)
   land with R43 (e) so the dialogs never promise a deletion the server does not yet make. The executor does not start a
   blocked step, does not fill a gap itself, and reports any premise it finds missing instead of choosing one.
3. `Map.tsx` and the census gate code of §16.2 are not touched; a defect found there is reported, not fixed. Gate and policy files of
   AC46 are Opus's.

**Status for the executor:** with R37 (b)–(e), R43 (b)–(e), R45 (b)–(e) and R46 (c)–(d) still waiting, `PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED` with the evidence

### 31.1 What the answers settle, and Opus's reading

- **D46, D52 (Q1).** A guest and a signed-in visitor see the same sold or rented listing. The owner confirmed Opus's reading
  (D52): archived, inactive, pending and expired listings stay visible to their owner and to staff only, and the profile page is a
  separate task. `noindex` moves from archived (C662) to sold and rented, once `archived_noindex_days` have passed since
  `updated_at`. D9 is amended in one point: every visitor's contact card shows the owner's name, avatar and a link to the profile
  page; the phone, WhatsApp and the inquiry stay closed.
- **D53 (Q2, replaces D47).** Moderation is for active listings only. An owner's edit of an active listing sends it to moderation.
  An edit at any other status (sold, rented, inactive, expired) is saved as it is, with no status change and no moderation. A
  listing goes through moderation when it becomes active again; that holds already, because only staff make a listing active (D8,
  C665). Under D46 a sold or rented listing is public, so its edited text is public without moderation; that is the owner's choice.
- **D54 (Q3).** Yes. The e-mail change and the person's own deletion need the current password, or a fresh Google sign-in for an
  account with no password. In the cabinet the password replaces the typed word DELETE (C689); the admin panel keeps the word (D34).
- **D55 (Q4).**
  - The switches are not secret values: a name such as `users.edit` gives an attacker nothing. What has to be protected is who can
    change them and who can read them.
  - Today a browser session can neither read nor write them, as a guest or signed in (C683). A switch changes only through the
    server, after an administrator check (C684), and every change is recorded.
  - Two gaps remain, and R75 closes both: a moderator can read the switches (C685), and four row policies on the table are
    unused. An unused policy opens the table silently the day someone grants a right on it.
- **D49 (Q5).** No caps per person (R76).
- **D50, D56, D58 (Q6, Q8).**
  - A person's own deletion stays immediate (C674, D30).
  - The 3-month reminder stays.
  - At 12 months the account is deactivated and the person is told by e-mail that it will be deleted in 30 days. The person
    signs in again only through the e-mail's "Activate account" button, which leads to the login page.
  - Today two things work against this: a marked account restores itself when the person comes back (C688, C295), and the last
    e-mail only links to the sign-in page (C687).
  - A listing stays active about 4 months: an e-mail 3 months after publication or edit, then deactivation 30 days later unless
    the owner extends it. Today it silently expires after 30 days (C675–C677).
  - Both flows need new e-mails, new screens and, for the account, new stored data. They become two separate tasks (31.3). Until
    they ship, nothing is deactivated, deleted or expired by a job (R77 (c), (d)), so nothing disappears silently in the meantime.
- **D51, D57 (Q7).**
  - The providers screen goes, and iliria98.com becomes the only source. A currency it does not publish is today derived from
    open.er-api.com (C679); that path goes.
  - No API key is involved anywhere: the rates are read from iliria98's public page (C680) and refreshed every hour with no one's
    action (C681). There is nothing to rotate.
  - One real gap: when the page cannot be read, no prices are converted at all (C682). R79 keeps the last good rates instead.
  - R78 (c)'s test keeps an unused screen from coming back.

### 31.3 The three tasks Opus creates after this revision, in this order, and what each inherits

1. **Listing lifecycle (D56).**
   - The clock starts when a listing becomes active (approval) and restarts on every later approval.
   - At 90 days the owner gets an e-mail in the account's language. Its link opens the listing in the cabinet, signed in.
   - "Still active" there restarts the clock, with no moderation: the content is unchanged.
   - Without it, 30 calendar days after the e-mail the listing becomes `expired` through the gateway as a system actor: hidden,
     and visible to its owner only. It becomes active again only through moderation (D53).
   - One e-mail per cycle, recorded so that a missed run neither skips nor repeats it.
   - Existing active listings get the new clock from the release, so none expires under the old 30 days. The job of R77 (d) then
     resumes.
2. **Account deactivation and activation (D58).** A security task. The threats and rules it must pin with unit tests:
   - **Mail scanners.** A mail scanner may open the link. So the link only opens the login page (`/auth/login?activate=<token>`),
     and nothing changes on a GET.
   - **What activation needs.** Activation needs both the e-mail's token and the account's password (or a Google sign-in of the
     same account). A stolen mailbox alone, or a password alone, is not enough.
   - **Error answers.** A wrong password gets the same answer as for any account, so nobody learns that an account is
     deactivated. A correct password without a token says the account is deactivated and offers a new e-mail to the account's
     own address, under the existing resend limit.
   - **The token.**
     - 32 random bytes, stored only as a SHA-256 hash, used once, valid until the deletion moment.
     - A new token voids the old one.
     - On arrival the token is moved from the URL into an `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` cookie for `/auth`, valid
       30 minutes.
     - The page sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` and `Cache-Control: no-store`.
     - The token is never logged and never reaches Sentry: the `activate` parameter is scrubbed.
   - **Wrong account.** A token for another account is refused with the generic answer. It is not used up, and the attempt is
     logged by user id only.
   - **Race with deletion.** Activation and the day-30 deletion both compare and set the account's state, so exactly one wins.
     The deletion is D30's complete deletion (R43).
   - **While deactivated.** Sessions are ended at once (R65 (c)), and the person has no access. The profile page is not found,
     the listings are hidden (today they are archived, C686), and the contact function refuses. No other e-mail is sent.
   - **After activation.**
     - The account is active, the reminder mark is cleared and the visit is recorded.
     - The listings hidden by the deactivation return to the statuses recorded at deactivation (D59).
     - A listing that was active comes straight back as active only if its content is the approved content. The test: its
       `updated_at` equals the value recorded at deactivation, and that value is not later than its last approval. Any other
       listing that was active goes to `pending` (D53).
     - The lifecycle clock of task 1 restarts at activation, so a returning listing is not expired by the days it spent hidden.
   - **The e-mail.** It holds only the greeting name and the link, over HTTPS.
   - **Stored data.** One table, service role only, no grant to `anon` or `authenticated`. It holds the user, the token hash,
     the deactivation time, the deletion time, the use time, and each hidden listing's recorded status and `updated_at`. The
     harness proves a session cannot read it.
   - **Q9 (answered, D59).** A listing that was active returns as active at once, provided its owner did not change it and it
     was approved.
3. **Public profile page (D46, D52, R73 (c)).** The card's profile link and the guest card are part of it. GR-7 reference study,
   UI contracts and Stories. The sold / rented switch is off by default, and its state lives in the URL.

## 38. Revision 19 — the owner's answers of 2026-10-21: v7.1 in production now, its release, and bots on the contact actions

The owner answered Q11 (D62: apply v7.1 now, v8 right after it). The apply target is production (D63). Bots must not be able to
use the contact actions (D64). The release is part of this task (D65).

Opus checked what production runs (`HEAD`, `rv24-08`) against v7.1. **Two HEAD paths break, and one of them is a security
regression:**
1. `createListing` still has the old generator (C748), so 57% of titles would be refused once the INSERT rule exists.
2. `getBlockedError` reads the person's own status row with the person's session (C749) and treats a missing row as allowed
   (C750). v7.1 hides that row from a blocked or deleted person (C751). With HEAD's code, every server action that checks the
   block and then writes with the service role would let a blocked person act. The v7.1 header already requires this change in
   the same release (C752).

Opus also inspected these and found them compatible: `updateListing` sends no protected column; the view route calls
`record_listing_view` through the service role; HEAD's `users` upserts are INSERTs that no policy allows, today and after.

**One release (D68, D69).** Task 923 ships in one push, made only when the whole task is approved (D68). v7.1 is applied to the
database now (D69), while the live site still runs `HEAD`. Until that push the live site keeps the two breaks above; D69 accepts
them because every account is a test account (D67). The working tree already holds both fixes (C742, C753), and every check of
Task 923 runs locally from the one project folder.

**The contact actions are open to bots twice over.** The phone reveal calls the contact function with the session client (C754).
Any signed-in session may also execute that function directly through the Data API (C755), so a bot does not need the button at
all. A human check is therefore real only on the server **and** with the session path closed in SQL. The project already
verifies Turnstile on the server (C756) and has one widget component (C757), so both are reused and no second bot product is added.

## 49. Review 29 and Revision 27 — the v8a dry run stopped at preflight 03, 2026-10-21

### 49.1 Review 29

The owner's dry run stopped at preflight 03: "the policy Admin/moderator delete avatars on storage.objects changed since the
capture" (C852). The preflight raises before any statement that changes the database, so nothing changed.

**The database did not change.** Opus compared the nine policies v8a touches with `catalog-post-v71.json` in a read-only
transaction (C854). All nine are equal, the policy of preflight 03 among them (C855, C856). Its live text spans several lines
with LF line breaks and has no carriage return (C855).

**The defect is in the check.** Preflight 03 compares that text with a SQL literal that spans several lines (C857). Preflights
01 and 02 compare one-line texts and passed, and preflight 03 is the first check of a text that spans several lines (C853).
The file reaches the editor through the clipboard (C860), and on the way the line breaks inside the literal change. The
literal then no longer equals the stored text. The rollback's end checks compare the same kind of literal (C858). So a
rollback pasted the same way would also stop, and v8a could not be undone. The function checks already compare an md5
(C859), and a paste cannot change a 32-character hex value.

**Opus's miss (process).** Review 28 checked that the texts were right, but not that they survive the owner's paste. A
check that compares text with the catalogue now compares an md5 of it, and its proof runs the text with both kinds of line
break.

**C839, C840 and C841 are withdrawn.** The owner does not run those files. R99 writes the new files, and Opus reviews their
hashes.

### 54.1 Opus's design choices

1. **The ceilings (D71).** A per-currency map lives in `src/modules/listings/validations/index.ts`. It is the one source for the schema, the form and the server. `price_old` is set by the server (C914), and the schema bounds it the same way.
2. **The price field (D73)** changes behaviour only, on the retained legacy `Input` of `ListingFormShellView` (C904). Task 907 moves that form to canonical Mantine (C905), and no canonical number field exists (C906). A Mantine field now would give one form two looks for the same meaning, so the parsing goes into a pure domain helper that Task 907 reuses. Review 32's note "the fix needs a canonical owner" is answered this way: the canonical owner of the behaviour is the helper, and the field's look stays with the form until Task 907.
3. **The restricted page (D72) is a COMPOSE:** `ListingsPageFrame` (C929) and `MantineEmptyLoadingErrorState` (C926–C928, C930) in one new View with its own Story. No new token, style or visual value. Three further decisions:
   - **The owner and staff open their listing in every non-public status, not only archived** (D52, D72). The cabinet links each of the owner's listings to its page (C925), and v8a lets the owner read it (C915). Otherwise the page would tell the owner that the owner had restricted it.
   - **A guest gets a "Sign in" action instead of a redirect**, so the owner, signed out, can still reach the listing.
   - **The page learns that a hidden listing exists through a server-only helper** on the admin client (C931). The helper returns one of three words and no listing field. The page tells a visitor that the address is a real listing, which D72 accepts (review 32 §6, the note to F11).
   - The existing `listing.access_denied_*` keys belong to another meaning and have no consumer (C932). They are not reused.

## 57. Review 36 and Revision 33 — R86: one contact gateway with a human check, 2026-10-22

**Review 36 (R108–R109 accepted).** The full record is the section "Review 36" of
`docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`. The owner's local-site check passed, so F16 is closed. This
revision is §54's step 5. It implements R86 (a), (b), (d), (e) and the gateway half of (c). The other half of (c) is
v8b's revoke of `get_listing_owner_contact` from `authenticated`, which stays with v8b after the push. R86 (f) is
unchanged.

**R78 (c) moves to its own revision, Revision 34, which comes right after this one.** §53 put both halves of R78 (c) into
the R86 revision. Its second half covers ten tables that only admin code writes (C1044). Several of their readers live in
admin libraries used outside admin, and four are audit tables that need to be classified. That work shares no file with
the gateway. D70 does not change. The order of §54 does not change, except that Revision 34 comes before R83.

### 57.1 What Opus established

- **Today's paths.**
  - The phone reveal is a public Server Action that calls the contact function through the session (C754, C978, C991).
  - A WhatsApp tap is recorded by a second client call to another public action (C979, C993).
  - The message action has no human check (C983).
  - The server check accepts any answer whose `success` is true. It checks neither the action nor the hostname (C985).
  - Cloudflare says to check both (C1023). A token is single-use, is valid for 300 s, and a replay is refused (C1020–C1022).
- **The database side is in place.** Hardening v8a is applied. Only the service role may execute
  `get_listing_owner_contact_as(p_caller, listing_id_param)`. It refuses a missing caller and a caller without access
  with 42501 (C1012–C1014).
  - §48's binding requirement holds: the caller's id comes only from the server's own Supabase Auth check (C984), never

  - The existing `CaptchaWidget` renders the flexible size (C988). That size needs at least 300 px (C1015).
  - The contact card is 246 px wide at 320 and 286 px at 360 (C1029, C1030), so a flexible challenge overflows it

    it still takes a flex slot, so it adds one gap (C1026).

  - The installed library 1.5.2 obtains a token on demand: `execute`, then `getResponsePromise` (C1008–C1011).
  - Execute mode issues no token before `execute` and a fresh one after each reset (C1036–C1038).
  - So every press gets one fresh token. That token cannot expire while the page stays open, and it is never reused.

  - A passing test answer carries the hostname `example.com`, no action, and the marker `result_with_testing_key`
    (C1033).
  - The failing secret and the spent-token secret answer as documented (C1034, C1035, C1025).

  - Both surfaces already show every failed contact as an error toast (C992, C995).

## 59. Review 38 and Revision 35 — R115–R116 accepted; R117–R120: Show number, the WhatsApp fallback and a check that answers at once, 2026-10-23

**Review 38.** The full record is the section "Review 38" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- R115 and R116 are accepted.
- The one lint failure of `r34-02` was in Opus's own Review 37 probe, and Opus fixed it.

**This revision.** It carries out the owner's decisions D75, D76 and D78 and corrects F22 and F23 (Review 37 addenda).
- The limits on number reveals (D77, D79, D80) need a reveal record in the database. They are Revision 36, right after this one.

### 59.1 What Opus established

- **Why WhatsApp and the call did not always open (F22).**
  - The container opens WhatsApp (C1069) and dials (C1070) only after the human check and the gateway have answered.
  - A browser lets a script open a window only while the click's activation lasts. In Chromium that activation is gone 5.5 s after the click (C1071).
  - The check and the gateway together often take longer than that.
- **Why a failed check took 30 s (F23).**
  - Every token request starts a new Cloudflare execution (C1072) and waits for the library's default 30 s (C1074).
  - The error handler drops Cloudflare's error code (C1073), although the library passes it (C1075). So an error is seen only at the timeout, and its cause is never recorded.
- **The design keeps the bot protection (D76).** The server check of R110–R111 does not change: one single-use token per gateway call, bound to the action and the hostname.
  - **Show number.** It needs no window. The number is shown in the card once the gateway answers.
  - **WhatsApp.** The token is requested in the background when the card mounts (C1076), so a press waits for the gateway only. When the activation has still expired by the time the number arrives, the card shows a link and a note instead (D78). Nothing fails silently.
- **The desktop toast.** It is raised and visible at 1440 px (C1080). The owner's "no toast on desktop" is the silent path of F22, which this revision removes.
- **Canonical decision (GR-0).**
  - `MantineListingContactPattern`: EXTEND, with two optional public props for the revealed number and the WhatsApp fallback. The note reuses the pattern's own dimmed extra-small text (C1079).
  - `CaptchaWidget`: EXTEND, with an opt-in `prefetch`.
  - `ListingContact`: REUSE.
  - No new token, value, wrapper or component. Token owner: `src/design-system/mantine/theme.ts`.
  - Reference research (GR-7): the visible change is the owner's own decision D75/D78 on the inherited card. The look of the buttons does not change.
- **The pending state of R116 stays** (C1081). A press of the other button while a request runs stays ignored (C1082): one token at a time.

This is the third finding of this class after F20 and F26. From this revision on, every proof command names its own baseline, and no command names a pinned file.

**This revision.** It adds the reveal limits that the owner decided:
- D77: 20 per hour and 60 per day per account;
- D79: 35 per hour and 120 per day per verified account;
- D80: 60 per hour and 200 per day per IP address.

D77 replaces D49 for contact reveals only, and R76 is amended the same way (C1128). Saved searches, collections and favourites stay without a cap. D64's protection of the contact actions from bots stays, and the limits add to it.

### 61.1 What Opus established

- **There is no limit today.** The gateway's fixed order has no limit (C1129). It refuses a listing without a number (C1130) and records the WhatsApp event after the lookup (C1131).
- **A limit needs a record of every reveal.** The new table `public.listing_contact_reveals` follows the task's own precedent, `public.reauth_failures` (C1137, C1138):
  - row level security is on, and no policy exists;
  - only the service role holds select, insert and delete;
  - anon and authenticated are revoked explicitly, because Supabase's default privileges would give them every privilege (C1139).
  - The table does not exist yet (C1136). Both keys it references are uuid (C1140, C1141).
  - The three SQL files parse (C1144, C1145). Their hashes are C1146–C1148. The dry-run file differs from the apply file in its last line only.
  - Opus checked the preflight's conditions with read-only SELECTs. The statements themselves are proved by the owner's dry run, which rolls back.
- **What is counted.** One row per listing that a viewer has not had revealed in the last 24 hours:
  - A repeat reveal of the same listing within 24 hours is free and writes no row. That viewer already knows the number.
  - Show number and WhatsApp of one listing count once.
  - The windows are the last hour and the last 24 hours, rolling, as in the message limit.
- **Verified.** "Verified" in D79 is the column `public.users.is_verified` (C1134, C1135): a boolean, never null, false by default. The gateway reads it for the viewer that Supabase Auth verified, never from the request.
- **The IP address.** It is the first address of `x-forwarded-for`, then `x-real-ip`, as in the message limit (C1142). A request with neither shares one bucket: the rows whose `requester_ip` is null.
- **Fail closed.** A count or flag that cannot be read, or a row that cannot be written, refuses the reveal, as in the message limit (C1143).
- **Retention.** The gateway deletes rows older than 48 hours. The 24-hour window needs no more.
- **The refusal.** It reuses the container's refusal toast (C1132, C1133) with a new text.
- **Canonical decision (GR-0).** `ListingContact`: REUSE (one more refusal text). `MantineListingContactPattern`: unchanged. No new component, token, prop or Story.

## 68. Revision 42 — R139: a deleted user's admin page opens the Users list with a notice, 2026-10-24

**The owner's request.** During Task 927's local AC12 (session record, "Owner's local AC12 of Task 927, part 3"):
- the owner had user 2's admin page open as user 1;
- user 2 then deleted their account;
- user 1's admin panel showed the 404 page.

The owner asked for the Users list instead (D85) and chose an explanation above it (D86).

**Today.** The admin user page calls `notFound()` in two cases: when no `users` row exists (C1228), and when the row has `deleted_at` (C1229). Its first await is the staff check (C1230), and the guard test SEC-X-SRV-ADMINPAGE-GUARD proves that order for every admin page (C1242, C1247, C1254). The users list already reads the query string (C1232) and its texts from `admin.pages` (C1231). Its header is `AdminPageHeader` (C1233). Both pages are in the D8_D9 scope (C1244, C1245); the header and its Story are not (C1246).

**Canonical decision (GR-0: EXTEND).**
- **Searched for:** a page-level notice under an admin page header, and an info message.
- **The notice itself is the canonical Mantine `Alert`:**
  - the theme maps the info meaning to `blueLight` (C1237) and owns the radius and variant (C1238);
  - its direct Story is `Mantine/Primitives/Alert` (C1240);
  - an admin Alert takes its icon size from `theme.other.iconSize.standard` (C1239);
  - its root carries `role="alert"` (C1243).
- **Its place is the shared `AdminPageHeader`:**
  - it is one `Box` with the `xl` margin below the dashboard header (C1234) and has no notice prop (C1235);
  - the gap is extended there, not in the route, so the page writes no spacing of its own;
  - the notice follows the header's own rhythm token `md` (C1236);
  - its direct Story is `Patterns/Mantine/AdminPageHeader` (C1241).
- **Registration:** the header is already in the migration scope (C1250). It is not newly enrolled, so no UI-contract row is required (C1251).

**Reference research (GR-7): inherited canonical design — owner decision 2026-10-20.** Every visual decision is covered by the theme's info Alert, `MantineDashboardHeader` and `AdminPageHeader`.

**Mobile.** The header's family is `structural-layout-and-feedback`, with `linear-flow` through `responsive-props` (C1248, C1249). Below 640 px the dashboard header already stacks its title and actions; the notice is one more full-width block of that column, and its text wraps.

## 70. Review 49 and Revision 44 — deletion v4 applied by the owner and verified; R141–R144: one complete deletion of an account in code, 2026-10-24

**Review 49 and the apply.** The full record is the section "Review 49" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- R140 is accepted.
- The owner approved the SHA-256 values in writing, ran the dry run, and then applied deletion v4. The dry run left nothing behind (C1291).
- Opus's read-only check of the applied database passes every check (C1281):
  - a report keeps the reporter's name (C1282);
  - a status history row and a reply keep their rows when the staff member goes (C1283, C1284);
  - the person's own views go with the account (C1285), and the count trigger runs as its owner (C1288);
  - a company goes with its creator (C1286).
- No key from a public table to a user blocks a deletion (C1287). The profile goes with the Auth user (C1329), and the listings, their image rows and the verification requests go with the profile (C1330, C1289, C1331).
- **Open obligation O1 (final review, owner decision).** The step 4 copy of §69.3 was not made: `supabase/migrations/` does not exist.
  - The repository also ignores the whole `/supabase` folder (C1344), so neither that copy nor the R37 (d) hardening copy could be committed.
  - The applied SQL is tracked in `docs/sessions/evidence/task923/db-catalog/` with its approved SHA-256.
  - Whether the migration history moves into Git is the owner's decision at the final review. R141–R144 do not depend on it.

**What the code does today.**
- Both deletions archive the listings first (C1293, C1297).
- Then they delete the profile row before the Auth user (C1294, C1298).
- So each has a branch in which the profile is gone and the Auth user stays (C1295, C1299). The cabinet shows its own text for it (C1305, C1310).
- No file of the person is released.
- `softDeleteUser` is mentioned only by tests outside its own body (C1300).
- The admin dialog still promises that the listings are archived (C1306, C1307), and its first point names only the profile data (C1308). The cabinet text says the same (C1309).

**What is already done, and what is no longer asked:**
- R46 (a) and (b) are done: the modal's typed confirmation (C1302) and its direct Story (C1303).
- R46 (c) is replaced by D54: the cabinet asks for the password (C1304), and SEC-DEL-FE-DENY and SEC-DEL-FE-ALLOW prove it.
- The inactivity part of R43 (d) is replaced by D58: the inactivity job deletes no account (C1301). The account lifecycle task will carry that deletion, so case SEC-DEL-INT-CRON leaves this contract.

**The design (R43 (c)–(e), R60, R62 (d)).**
- **Order.** `auth.admin.deleteUser` removes the Auth user, the profile and every dependent row in one transaction (C1329, C1287).
- **Files.** Each Cloudinary id is collected first, because the rows that hold the URLs go with the account. A file is released only after the rows are gone, so the reference check passes.
  - The ids come from the URLs, as listing deletion takes them (C1314).
  - A failed read refuses, as listing deletion does (C1315).
  - Release goes through `deleteAsset`:
    - it is a dry run unless the delete mode is enabled (C1316);
    - it keeps a file whose reference check fails (C1317);
    - it throws when Cloudinary fails (C1318).
  - A failed file never undoes the deletion. It is counted.
- **Storage.** The project has one Storage bucket, `avatars` (C1290). The test double of the database has no Storage API (C1328), so the unit test of `deleteAccount` builds its own double.

**Canonical decision (GR-0: REUSE)** for the admin dialog:
- The canonical modal already owns the typed confirmation (C1302) and its direct Story (C1303), and the typed state has its own census row (C1336).
- The admin dialog passes one documented public prop and a locale label. No visual value is written.
- The modal's UI-contract row (C1335) and the dialog view's migration scope (C1334) do not change.
- The census rows of the `Delete` and `DeleteLoading` Stories open on mount and trap focus (C1337). Neither changes.
- The typed value is the modal's own state, not a prop, so a Story cannot set it. The primitive's census row exercises it.

**Reference research (GR-7): inherited canonical design — owner decision 2026-10-20.** R46 (e) records why a typed word is used (D34).

**Mobile.** The modal belongs to the `overlay-and-disclosure` family (C1332, C1333). Below 640 px it keeps its canonical presentation; the typed field is one more full-width section of the modal.

**Review 53.** The full record is the section "Review 53" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- **The owner's check (C1402–C1407).**
  - The `Delete` dialog in Storybook passes.
  - The owner deleted the test user from the admin panel of lero.al (C1405). lero.al runs the pushed code (C1407), whose `hardDeleteUser` asks for no typed word and releases no file (C1406). So no DELETE was asked and the photos stayed in Cloudinary. Task 923's deletion asks for DELETE (R144) and releases every file (C1408), and it reaches lero.al with §65's one push.

- **F18 (P1, task design: R45).** The open tab of a deleted account stays signed in and loops (C1402, C1403).
  - The server ends the session on the next request (C1393), and its reads find no user (C1392).
  - The browser keeps the state it was given when the page first loaded (C1394, C1395). Nothing re-checks it on a client navigation, and a token refresh does not re-check it (C1396). So the header still shows the person signed in, against D29.

The bridge acts on the stale `authenticated` status and sends the person back to the cabinet (C1389, C1390). This repeats without end.
  - SEC-D29-FE-DENY proves only a page loaded after the session ended (C1401), not an open tab.
  - The same holds for a banned or deactivated account whose tab is open.

## 74. Review 54 and Revision 48 — R147 accepted in code but for F19; R148: a re-check that React Strict Mode cut off is started again, 2026-10-24

**Review 54.** The full record is the section "Review 54" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- **R147 in code.** (a)–(d) were traced through the bridge, the provider and the controller (C1415–C1420).
  - Opus reran r47-01's 20 files: 605 of 606 tests pass (C1431). Typecheck and eslint exit 0 (C1438).
  - B10 and B11 fail on their intended assertions and are restored (C1432). The full run has no new failing ID (C1433).
  - An open tab that navigates into the sign-in page opens the sheet once, sends nobody on and ends as a guest, also under React Strict Mode, 5 s and 40 s after load (C1425). F18's loop is closed in code.
- **F19 (P2; implementation, and task design of R147 (a)).** Under React Strict Mode, a full load of the bridge with a signed-in first state never leaves the loader.
  - Next.js turns Strict Mode on for the App Router when the config does not set it (C1421, C1422). So `next dev`, where the owner's check runs, mounts, cleans up and mounts every effect once on a full load.
  - The bridge asks its re-check once (C1415). The provider's cleanup aborts that request (C1417, C1418), and the aborted re-check commits nothing (C1419, C1420). The bridge then waits for an answer that never comes (C1416), and the status stays `refreshing` (C1423).
  - The sign-up page renders the bridge with no server check (C1413). A signed-in person who opens `/auth/register` in a new tab stays on the loader; before R147 they reached the cabinet. Under root Strict Mode the saved SEC-D29-FE-STALE-ALLOW (i) fails the same way (C1424).
  - Task design: R147 (a) took the bridge's comment (C1414) as its premise, and the sign-up page breaks it.
  - A production build has no Strict Mode, so lero.al would not be affected.
  - The saved test's fetch double ignores the abort signal (C1437); a browser rejects an aborted request.
- **F20 (P3, task design: AC147).** r47-01 requires `controller.test.ts` to pass. One of its cases is red in both baselines, on an unmocked fetch (C1428–C1430). Sonnet reported it correctly; AC148 names it.
- **Correction.** AC147 said that four Stories mount `AuthProvider`. None does (C1434). `npm run build-storybook` stays required as the final build of the task.
- **The builds.** Sonnet stopped correctly at the dev-server check (C1435). Neither server runs now (C1436). The builds run once, after R148.

## 75. Review 56 and Revision 49 — the owner's admin deletion passes; R149: an absent account is not logged as a failed query, 2026-10-25

**Review 56.** The full record is the section "Review 56" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- **The owner's check, first item (C1443, C1444, C1446).** The admin deletion on `http://localhost:3000` released the listing photo (`outcome: 'DELETED'`), the photo left Cloudinary, and the account has no Auth user.
- **F21 (P3; implementation of the page, and task design of R139's test double).** After the deletion, DevTools shows a console error (C1440, C1441).
  - The deletion's request is served on the profile page (C1445). The page looks the account up with `.single()` (C1449), which answers an absent row with PostgREST's no-row error PGRST116 (C1442, C1447).
  - The page logs every lookup error (C1450), so an account that is merely gone is logged as a failed query. The page still opens the Users list with the notice (C1451): only the log is wrong.
  - `.maybeSingle()` answers an absent row with no row and no error (C1448).
  - The saved GONE case's double answers an absent account with no error, unlike PostgREST (C1453, C1454), and the test silences `console.error` without asserting it (C1455). With a double that answers as PostgREST does, today's page logs PGRST116 (C1457).
- The page's metadata also reads with `.single()` but logs nothing (C1452), so it is unchanged.

An absent account then answers no row and no error (C1448). The state holds the row (or null) and the failure (or null) instead of one answer. `single()` answers the failure if one is set, else the row, else `{ data: null, error: { code: 'PGRST116', details: 'The result contains 0 rows', hint: null, message: 'Cannot coerce the result to a single JSON object' } }`. `maybeSingle()` answers the failure if one is set, else the row or null with no error. The `users` chain supports `select`, `eq`, `single` and `maybeSingle`; any other call still throws.<br>- SEC-X-SRV-ADMIN-USER-GONE also asserts `expect(console.error, 'an absent account is not a failed query').not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.<br>- SEC-X-SRV-ADMIN-USER-QUERY-ERROR also asserts, with the message `a failed lookup is still logged`, that `console.error` was called once with `'AdminUserProfilePage: user query failed'` and an object containing that failure and the id.<br>- DELETED and PRESENT keep their assertions. ## 76. Revision 50 — password sign-in, the server's password check and the test users under Supabase's CAPTCHA protection, 2026-10-25

**Why.** The full record is the section "Task 927 Review 4" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`.
- Supabase Auth's CAPTCHA protection is on, in production too, and production and development are linked (D87, D88). It refuses every password sign-in that carries no token (C1460).
- A Google ID-token sign-in and a refresh are not refused (C1461, C1462). A service-role caller passes, and its verify session ends cleanly (C1464, C1465).
- R67 (c) relies on this protection for sign-up and reset (C1468). Three password paths do not carry a token:
  - **The sheet's password sign-in.** It sends the e-mail and the password only, in the pushed code (C1470) and in the working tree (C1473, C1474). So every e-mail sign-in fails.
  - **The server's password check.** E-mail change, deletion and password change use a verify client with the anon key (C1472, C1481). It is refused for the right password (C1463), and the refusal is counted as a wrong password (C1482).
  - **The test users.** The fixtures sign synthetic users in with the anon key (C1484). The 15 real-boundary suites that need one fail at the fixture (C1467). They passed on 2026-10-24, before the protection was on (C1466).
- The pushed sign-up also hands Supabase a token that its own Cloudflare check has already used (C1471, C1469).

**Owner action now, outside this route.** The owner turns the CAPTCHA protection off. The pushed code needs it off: its sign-up and reset check Turnstile themselves. After the deploy of the push, the owner turns it on again (§76.3, step 5).

## 77. Review 58 and Revision 51 — R150–R155 accepted; R156: a password change ends every session, the check's own included, 2026-10-25

**Review 58.** The full record is the section "Review 58" of `docs/sessions/2026-10-10-task923-rendered-state-census.md`, with the owner's local checks.
- R150–R155 and AC150 are accepted.
- The owner's local checks pass for the e-mail sign-in, a wrong password and the cabinet deletion.
- **F22 (P2; implementation of S55, Revision 7, unchanged by R153).** After the cabinet password change, the browser's global sign-out got no answer (C1487). The SDK logs every Auth request that fails that way (C1488). Supabase does send CORS headers on these answers, so CORS is not the cause (C1489, C1490).
  - After the password check, the verify client's session is the check's own (C1491). So `signOut({ scope: 'others' })` (C1498) ends the browser's and every other session, and keeps the check's own alive (C1492, C1493).
  - The browser's own global sign-out cannot end it either (C1494). Every password change therefore leaves one live session behind, against S55's case (C1503).
  - It also signs out with the browser's session already ended, which is the request the owner's browser cut off (C1487).
  - A global sign-out through the request's session client ends all three sessions and empties the browser's auth cookie (C1495, C1496). With no session stored, the SDK's sign-out sends no request (C1497).
- The deleted user's second browser (§75.2) shows the same SDK log after a navigation (C1488, C1490). Whether that browser then shows the guest header without a loop is still to be confirmed by the owner; it is not part of R156.
